verdict.rationale: Ghostty is a local terminal application that runs entirely on the user's own machine. The source is on GitHub and community members report building it themselves on Debian/Ubuntu and via the project's Nix flake. It is also distributed through distro repositories and an official .dmg, and its core library (libghostty) is reusable by anyone. Hands-on reports note friction: missing GTK/libadwaita dev packages, no .deb package, and Ubuntu 22.04's GTK4 being too old. Missing for 10: explicit open-source license evidence in the pack, first-party build-from-source documentation, smoother build experience on older distros.
